about: The real-model picking test (TOOL_ACCESS_PLAN §7.2, scripts/eval-tools.ts), written on 2026-11-27 in stage 0. A model gets the web door's instructions and listed tools, then one user message; world is the user's data, which the tools' canned answers show it. kind: listed (the right tool is in today's web list of 32), found (it is not: find_tools, then use_tool or use_read_tool), none (nothing should change: plain talk, general knowledge, or a message where a confusable tool would be the wrong pick). expect: the tools any one of which, reached with valid inputs, passes the case ([] for none: it passes when nothing outside allowed changes). allowed: other changing tools that are fine to call as well; read tools are always allowed. A call to a changing tool outside expect and allowed is a wrong pick. ids, where the message points at things in the world: the right call acts on at least one of them (a subject, a goal or a project may be named by its name or key instead of its id). Doc ids are letters and digits only, as the schema wants. Messages are written the way people type to ChatGPT; no real people.
world: The user's data in this test. Docs: 'Kafka basics' (dockafka), 'Sliding window' (docsliding), 'System design: caching' (doccache), 'ERP notes' (docerp), 'Old scratch' (docold, in no subject).
